paragraphs: Direct assessment: being a lawyer is worth exploring further only if you are willing to verify client facts, evidence, legal sources and procedural deadlines, and take responsibility for uncertainty in advice, conflicts of interest, document versions and authorized issuance.

Observable signals: you can check facts and legal sources sentence by sentence, maintain records during contentious communication, explain unfavorable factors and tradeoffs, and escalate promptly under deadline pressure.

Safe work sample: use entirely fictional contract clauses, a factual timeline, assumptions and task constraints to produce an issue list, legal-source checklist, risk matrix and revision notes within 90 minutes; do not handle real cases, client facts, court documents or legal opinions.

Sample reflection: check whether you distinguish facts, legal issues, assumptions, deadlines and conclusions requiring confirmation by a practicing lawyer, and whether you can explain evidence gaps and authorization boundaries.

Lawyers research, interpret and apply law within their authorized jurisdictions and the scope of their engagement, representing or advising clients in litigation, transactions and other legal matters; this page does not extrapolate US occupational statistics into qualifications to practice in China.

entries: Research | Verify facts and legal sources | Take client accounts, evidence and applicable legal sources as inputs, distinguishing original statements, verified facts and assumptions; produce a list of issues and evidence, without presenting a lack of evidence as a definitive conclusion.

Documents | Drafting and client communication | Draft contracts, litigation documents or internal opinions under the engagement, explaining options, limitations and risks; produce documents with versions, citations and approvers, verifying authority before formal external issuance.

Representation | Engagement and procedural progress | Check engagement scope, conflicts and litigation or transaction deadlines, and organize negotiations and submissions; produce a deadline register and process records, with court appearances and issuance governed by jurisdiction and organizational authorization.

paragraphs: Key judgments: are facts supported by materials, are legal sources current and applicable to this matter, how are deadlines calculated, and are client wishes distinguished from feasible options? Refer conflicts, confidentiality issues and out-of-scope matters to the supervising lawyer or person responsible for the matter.

Environment and pace: law firms, in-house legal departments, government or public-interest organizations, usually with many deadlines and high standards for writing, communication and professional responsibility.

Working materials: legislation and case searches, document and version systems, evidence indexes and deadline registers; tools support research and organization, but cannot determine the applicability of legal sources, client instructions or authority to issue documents externally.
Collaboration chain: clients, legal teams, legal operations, experts, courts or arbitral institutions, counterparties and regulators.
Quality standards: traceable facts and legal sources, no missed deadlines, controlled conflicts of interest, advice that explains uncertainty, and documents reviewed and issued with authorization.

Boundaries with adjacent roles: lawyers provide regulated legal advice and representation; paralegals, legal compliance, mediation and arbitration, and contract management roles have distinct duties involving neutrality, support or processes.
Lawyers provide regulated legal advice and representation; paralegals focus on research and document support.
Legal compliance roles design control processes; lawyers take responsibility for legal interpretation and representation.
Arbitrators and mediators remain neutral; lawyers represent one party's interests.
Contract managers maintain commercial terms and performance processes; lawyers assess legal risk and enforceability.

Insufficient evidence: comparable accuracy rates, organizational adoption rates or causal occupational outcomes have not been obtained for lawyers' seven work directions. AI can assist with indexing materials, comparing contracts and drafting documents. ABA 512 discusses competence, confidentiality, client communication and supervision under US Model Rules; it cannot be treated as Chinese law. Users must still verify original facts and current legal sources, with authorized lawyers responsible for judgments and external issuance.
Lawyer wages in mainland China: industry references and specific gaps

The National Bureau of Statistics reports average annual wages of CNY 110162 in urban non-private units and CNY 68919 in private units in leasing and business services in 2025. These are broad industry annual averages before tax, rather than lawyers' medians, starting wages, city-specific monthly wages or partners' profit distributions. The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security's 2025 enterprise remuneration survey separately provides annual wages for the broad occupational group 207, “legal, social and religious professionals”: 10/25/50/75/90 percentiles of 3.69/5.50/8.40/15.61/24.60 ten thousand CNY. These are not lawyer-specific percentiles and cover a different population from NBS industry averages.

Insufficient evidence: national wage percentiles, city distributions and income at different practice stages have not been obtained for the specific occupation of lawyer in mainland China. Industry figures cannot price an individual's services; US lawyer statistics are listed separately.

Insufficient evidence: comparable causal data on how AI adoption affects individual lawyers' wages in China have not been obtained. Tool demonstrations, permission to use tools and US ethics opinions cannot establish changes in Chinese income.

items.title: What employers or responsible people will check

values: Material 1 | Delay clauses in a supply contract

Jurisdictional assumption: solely an exercise in contract analysis in mainland China; does not constitute legal advice or involve real cases. Party A purchases equipment and Party B supplies it. Clause 3.1: Party B must deliver by 2026-10-10 18:00. Clause 3.2: anticipated delays must be notified in writing within 2 working days of becoming aware of them, with reasons given.

Clause 4.1: liquidated damages accrue for each day of delay at 0.3% of the contract price of the undelivered portion, capped cumulatively at 5% of the contract price. Clause 6.2: force majeure, notification and proof are handled as agreed in the contract. Contract price: CNY 100,000; payment made: CNY 30,000; acceptance has not begun.
Material 2 | Factual timeline

On 2026-09-30, Party B emailed that “components may arrive late,” without proof; at 2026-10-10 18:00, delivery had not occurred; on 2026-10-11, Party A requested an explanation; on 2026-10-12, Party B stated that “supplier-related causes constitute force majeure,” still without proof; on 2026-10-14, Party B proposed partial delivery, with quantity and date undetermined.

Role and limitations: the participant may submit only an internal draft to a supervising lawyer, and may not send letters on a client's behalf, confirm breach, promise settlement or reach final legal conclusions.
Material 3 | Internal draft assignment

List known facts, facts requiring confirmation, contract clauses and legal issues requiring verification separately; indicate the significance of dates such as 2026-10-10 and 10-12, without inventing whether notice is compliant.

Write a one-page internal memorandum for a supervising lawyer: raise five groups of questions about delivery/notice/force majeure/liquidated damages/partial delivery, explain necessary evidence and next steps, and leave determinations of whether claims are established to applicable legal sources and the supervising lawyer's review.
Material 4 | Reference approach and boundaries

Suggested columns: 3.1, delivery deadline of month 10, day 10, 18:00 is known, and the scenario states that delivery did not occur; 3.2, verify email sending and receipt, time of awareness, the definition of working days and compliance of content; 6.2, “supplier-related causes” alone cannot establish force majeure—obtain proof and applicable legal sources; 4.1, the base is the undelivered portion, the daily rate is 0.3% and the cap is 5% of the contract price, but days of delay and the undelivered amount still require confirmation; the quantity, timing and acceptance implications of partial delivery are unknown.

Do not assert that force majeure is established, liquidated damages are necessarily recoverable or partial delivery must be accepted; produce only an issue tree and evidence list. The materials are original fiction for paper analysis; do not contact real parties or send legal documents.

items.title: Entry case materials: use only the fictional materials on this page

values: Fact–clause timeline
Reuse Material 1, “Delay clauses in a supply contract,” and Material 2, “Factual timeline,” listing clause dates, email dates, delivery status and sources item by item; keep unknown matters unknown.
Issue tree and evidence list

Following Material 3, “Internal draft assignment,” separate five groups of issues: notice, force majeure, liquidated damages, partial delivery and acceptance, listing the contracts, emails and proof needed.
Internal memorandum draft
Prepare a one-page draft for a supervising lawyer, raising only verification questions and possible paths, without speaking for a client or making final conclusions.
Review record

Review the draft item by item against Material 4, “Reference approach and boundaries”; change actual overstatements back to questions requiring verification. If there are no errors, record the checks and reasons for retaining the text, without inventing revisions.

items.title: What may be checked during a trial task, probation or before delivery?

values: Day 1 | Read clauses
Read only Material 1, “Delay clauses in a supply contract,” marking 3.1/3.2/4.1/6.2 and payment and acceptance information; produce clause cards.
Day 2 | Arrange the timeline
Using Material 2, “Factual timeline,” record dates, speakers, events and sources; list “may arrive late” and “force majeure” separately as original statements.
Day 3 | List issues
Using Material 3, “Internal draft assignment,” build a five-group issue tree, distinguishing questions needing facts, contract interpretation and applicable legal sources.
Day 4 | Write an internal draft
Prepare an internal memorandum draft for a supervising lawyer, noting unresolved matters, evidence requests and the boundary that you do not represent a client.
Day 5 | Compare with the reference

After finishing the first draft, read Material 4, “Reference approach and boundaries,” and review item by item. Rewrite only sentences that actually present questions of whether a claim is established as definitive conclusions; if there are no errors, record check results and reasons for retaining the text.
Day 6 | Assemble the portfolio
Organize the timeline, issue tree, evidence list, internal draft and revision record, labeling them original fiction/paper exercise/no contact with parties.
Day 7 | Reflect and decide
Assess whether you are willing to keep checking facts, legal sources, deadlines, versions and review boundaries over the long term; do not assess personality or ability to practice law.

items.title: Seven-day low-cost experience: reuse the same set of materials

entries: Check item by item that the timeline comes only from Material 2, “Factual timeline”; do not invent component suppliers, receipt of notices or client intentions.
Check whether the notice obligation under 3.2 is separated from the force majeure issue under 6.2, and whether writing, deadlines and proof are listed as matters requiring verification.
Review whether the calculation conditions in 4.1 are recorded fully: undelivered portion, 0.3% per day and 5% cap; do not calculate the amount payable yourself.
Check whether the quantity, acceptance and client choices regarding partial delivery remain unknown, rather than stating that it must be accepted or necessarily constitutes breach.
Record your reaction to incomplete legal sources or facts: can you stop at an issue list, or do you rush to conclusions about winning litigation or breach?
Distinguish enjoying clause analysis from enjoying “deciding for others”; lawyers' work also requires confidentiality, authority, review and jurisdictional boundaries.
For the next step, choose only public learning materials with guidance and a clear jurisdiction; do not treat one paper draft as authorization to practice or a client outcome.

risks.consequence: Treating assertions as facts may misjudge responsibility and contaminate documents.
risks.mitigation: Create separate columns for facts/original statements/unknowns; trace each item to evidence and submit to the lawyer handling the matter for verification.
risks.scenario: The scenario email claims component delays without proof, or a client's account differs from original documents.

risks.consequence: Incorrect legal sources may leave opinions, documents or strategies without a valid basis.
risks.mitigation: Check primary legal sources, legal force and scope of application; remove fabricated citations and submit to the lawyer handling the matter for review.
risks.scenario: Citing outdated legislation, AI-fabricated cases or rules whose jurisdiction has not been checked.

risks.consequence: Notices may be missed or procedural deadlines exceeded; contractual deadlines are not litigation deadlines.
risks.mitigation: List deadline types, calculation bases and conditions needing verification separately; report immediately to the person responsible for the matter as a deadline approaches, without waiting for tool answers.
risks.scenario: Delivery dates, the start of notice periods or procedural deadlines have not been confirmed.

risks.consequence: May disclose protected information or take on matters where representation is prohibited.
risks.mitigation: Check confidentiality and conflicts first; stop unapproved external data transfers and report to the lawyer handling the matter and the head of the law firm.
risks.scenario: Client materials are proposed for tool input, or conflicts involving both sides of the same case / relatives have not been checked.

risks.consequence: Fabricated facts, quotations or commitments can mislead clients; automation cannot bear professional responsibility.
risks.mitigation: Label the draft and verify originals and quotations item by item; an authorized lawyer approves external issuance. For US ethics, separately check rules in the actual jurisdiction.
risks.scenario: An AI first draft is used directly as a formal legal opinion or sent to a client without approval.

risks.consequence: Out-of-scope commitments may cause quality problems or unauthorized practice.
risks.mitigation: Check the engagement contract, organizational acceptance and reviewer, explaining incomplete items; where necessary, ask the lawyer handling the matter to narrow scope or transfer it.
risks.scenario: The law firm's engagement scope, supervisor or current capacity to deliver is unclear.

source_card.note: Interpret sources according to their respective geography, period, occupational population and limitations. O*NET's custom page is an options entry; details/summaries support US lawyer tasks, recruitment software data are not AI adoption, and certification and training directories do not confer qualifications. NBS urban-unit wages and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security's enterprise remuneration survey are industry/broad occupational group references consulted for this page; precisely matched national wage distributions or demand volumes for Chinese lawyers have still not been obtained, which does not establish that official sources have never published them. BLS/O*NET wages and employment have different coverage. The Lawyers Law supports Chinese practice responsibilities; ABA provides ethics information under US Model Rules, NIST is a general risk framework, and NCBE is an entry point for jurisdictional admission inquiries. These sources cannot substitute for one another.

description.text: Lawyers turn client facts, evidence, legal texts, procedural deadlines, negotiation positions and conflict-of-interest information into legal analysis, opinions and documents, procedural submissions, negotiation plans, and court-hearing or transaction records. To assess this career path, verify the complete work cycle, responsibility boundaries, evidence scope, risk controls and observable entry-level portfolio work together.

subject.name: Lawyers
subject.summary: Lawyers provide legal analysis and advice based on client facts, evidence and legal rules, draft or submit legal documents, and represent or assist clients in litigation, transactions or other legal matters. To assess this path, check jurisdictional admission, traceability of facts and legal sources, deadlines, conflicts of interest and authorized issuance together.
